documents.title: Rule 111-8-63-.07 Owner Governance, paragraph (2). This is the list of required policies and procedures for Assisted Living Communities (25+ residents).
documents.issuer: Georgia Department of Community Health, Healthcare Facility Regulation Division (HFRD). Published by the Georgia Secretary of State, Rules & Regulations.
documents.version: Current text posted at rules.sos.ga.gov (Subject 111-8-63), fetched 10/14/2026. The page shows no effective date for .07.
documents.how_used: Main source for ALC policy content. .07(2) says the governing body must implement policies, procedures and practices that support dignity, respect, choice, independence and privacy in a safe environment. It also says the policies must, at a minimum, give direction to staff and residents on items (a) through (p). Georgia has no separate DCH policy checklist form, so this regulation section is the list.

documents.title: Rule 111-8-62-.07 Governing Body, paragraph (3). This is the list of required policies and procedures for Personal Care Homes (2–24 beds).
documents.issuer: Georgia Department of Community Health, Healthcare Facility Regulation Division (HFRD). Published by the Georgia Secretary of State, Rules & Regulations.
documents.version: Current text posted at rules.sos.ga.gov (Subject 111-8-62), fetched 10/14/2026. The page shows no effective date for .07.
documents.how_used: Main source for PCH policy content. .07(3) uses the same introductory language as the ALC rule and lists items (a) through (p). The PCH list is not identical to the ALC list: it has no separate rule items for ALC refunds order, staffing ratios for assisted self-preservation, or the ALC sub-list order. See the item text for the differences.

documents.title: Assisted Living Community Application Checklist (DCH HFRD), including the Affidavit of Compliance for Ch. 111-8-63
documents.form_number: No form number. The packet contains the ALC Application Checklist, the Affidavit of Compliance and the Affidavit of Financial Stability.
documents.issuer: Georgia DCH, Healthcare Facility Regulation Division
documents.version: Undated checklist. The Affidavit of Compliance is signed by Commissioner Dean Burke. Fetched 10/14/2026.
documents.how_used: This is the document the state uses at application. It does not list policy topics. Its 15 'Initial' items are all application paperwork and are excluded. It says all policies and procedures must be established under the regulations and be readily available on request. The notarized Affidavit of Compliance (Ch. 111-8-63) attests that the applicant has developed the mandated policies and procedures and will implement them immediately on licensure. The policy content is therefore taken from .07(2).

documents.title: Personal Care Home Application Checklist (DCH HFRD), including the Affidavit of Compliance for Ch. 111-8-62
documents.form_number: No form number. The packet contains the PCH Application Checklist and the Affidavit of Compliance (select Personal Care Homes).
documents.issuer: Georgia DCH, Healthcare Facility Regulation Division
documents.how_used: Same use as the ALC checklist. Its 14 'Initial' items are paperwork only and are excluded. It says policies and procedures must be established and readily available on request. The policy content is taken from 111-8-62-.07(3).

required_items.text: the services available in the assisted living community, including, personal services, assisted living care, memory care services and any other specialized services such as memory care centers and designated proxy caregivers;
the staffing plan that the community utilizes to ensure that staffing ratios increase proportionally as the number of residents who require assisted self-preservation increases;

admissions, discharges and immediate transfers which ensure that the community does not admit or retain residents who need more care that the assisted living community is authorized or capable of providing;
refunds when a resident is transferred or discharged;
training and ongoing evaluation of staff, including specialized training if designated proxy caregivers are provided or memory care is offered;
house rules and their enforcement;
protecting the rights of the residents as set forth in these rules;
medication management, procurement, the use of certified medication aides and professional oversight provided for such services;
health and hygiene issues for residents and staff relating to infection control, work policies and return to work policies, food borne illnesses and reportable diseases;

the investigation and reporting of abuse, neglect, exploitation of residents, residents' wandering away from the community, accidents, injuries and changes in residents' conditions to required parties;
discipline procedures for handling acts committed by staff which are inconsistent with the policies of the assisted living community;
emergency preparedness, drills and evacuation requirements;
quality assurance review mechanisms, including resident and family feedback to determine opportunities for improving care;
the use of volunteers and their orientation regarding resident's rights and basic safety precautions;

the specific use of proxy caregivers allowed within the community and the oversight of proxy caregivers the community requires or provides in accordance with Georgia law, these rules and the rules for proxy caregivers, Chapter 111-8-100; and

the safety and security precautions that will be employed by the assisted living community to protect residents from harm by other residents, designated proxy caregivers, and other individuals, not employed by the community who routinely come into the community.
The services available in the home, including, personal services, memory care services/centers and any other specialized services such as designated proxy caregivers.
Admissions, discharges and immediate transfers which ensure that the home does not admit or retain residents who need more care than the home is authorized or capable of providing.
Refunds when a resident is transferred or discharged.
Training and ongoing evaluation of staff, including specialized training if designated proxy caregivers are provided or memory care is offered.
House rules and their enforcement.
Protecting the rights of the residents as set forth in these rules;
Medication management, procurement and the professional oversight provided for such services.
Health and hygiene issues for residents and staff relating to infection control, work policies and return to work policies, food borne illnesses and reportable diseases.

The investigation and reporting of abuse, neglect, exploitation of residents, residents' wandering away from the community, accidents, injuries and changes in residents' conditions to required parties.
Discipline procedures for handling conduct which is inconsistent with the policies of the home committed by staff.
Emergency preparedness, drills and evacuation requirements.

Quality assurance and peer review mechanisms to determine opportunities for improving care utilizing information acquired from reports and investigations of serious incidents, including resident and family feedback.
The use of volunteers, who have unsupervised access to the residents and their orientation regarding resident's rights and basic safety precautions.

The specific use of proxy caregivers allowed within the home and the oversight of proxy caregivers the home requires or provides in accordance with Georgia law, these rules and the rules for proxy caregivers, Chapter 111-8-100.

The safety and security precautions that will be employed by the home to protect residents from harm by other residents, designated proxy caregivers and other individuals, not employed by the home who routinely come into the home.
The staffing plan which takes into account the specific needs of the residents and also includes arrangements for staffing in the absence of regularly scheduled staff.

sections: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p), in the rule's order
PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p), in the rule's order

notes: No single DCH policy-review form exists for Georgia ALCs or PCHs, so the rule sections above are used instead. The rule lists the topics only as lettered paragraphs with no headings, so use the lettered items as the manual's categories. Section names are not invented. Use the ALC list for 25+ beds (Ch. 111-8-63) and the PCH list for 2–24 beds (Ch. 111-8-62). The two lists differ in order and wording: the ALC list adds the certified medication aide reference in (h) and orders its staffing-ratio item as (b), while the PCH list puts the staffing plan last as (p). Both rules say the lists are a 'minimum', so they are not exhaustive. Other sections of Chapters 111-8-62 and 111-8-63 contain further written-policy or program requirements, such as resident rights, memory care and staff training. I did not read those sections in this pass, so I did not list them. Check them before finalizing a manual. Submission and review: the HFRD checklists do not ask for the policies manual to be uploaded in the GAHLES portal. Their 'Initial' items are application paperwork only (14 for PCH, 15 for ALC). Instead, the applicant signs a notarized Affidavit of Compliance for the applicable chapter (111-8-63 or 111-8-62). It attests that the policies and procedures have been developed and will be implemented immediately once licensed. DCH says licensed facilities face unannounced periodic inspections where the policies must be 'readily available' for review for sufficiency and compliance. Deficient policies may bring sanctions under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-25. The checklists also say all policies and procedures must be established and readily available upon request. The manual should therefore be organized item by item so each lettered paragraph can be found quickly during a survey. Fetched 10/14/2026. The checklist pages carry no revision dates, so re-check the DCH page before relying on them. The fetched PCH rule text was cut off partway through .08, which does not affect .07(3).
